title: How to (Accidentally) Spot a British Pakistani Aunty. Tip #1
body: She has a WhatsApp group with every woman from the mosque committee and it has arranged more marriages than any app ever will. Ask how she knows somebody and it involves a village back home, a school in Ilford, and a wedding in 2003. It's a sealed deal if she can trace two strangers to the same district in Punjab within four minutes.
caption:
Tip #1 😭 the freezer is a strategic reserve.

title: How to (Accidentally) Spot a British Pakistani Aunty. Tip #2
body: Watch the wedding shopping, because Green Street is not a street, it's an institution. Six trips, three of them just to look, and a shop where the owner brings out the good stock from the back because he knows the family. It's a sealed deal if she has bought gold from the same jeweller for twenty-five years and would not consider another one.

title: How to (Accidentally) Spot a British Pakistani Aunty. Tip #3
body: Ask about the freezer and understand that it is a strategic reserve. Samosas for forty. Curry portioned into containers with masking tape and dates. Somebody is always about to arrive and nobody will ever be fed inadequately. It's a sealed deal if a guest has been fed a full meal after saying, clearly, that they had already eaten.

title: How to (Accidentally) Spot a British Pakistani Aunty. Tip #4
body: Listen for the food exchange, because it runs the whole street. She sends a dish to three houses. Something comes back in the same container two days later, refilled. Nobody has discussed this system in eleven years. It's a sealed deal if a container has circulated so long that neither family remembers who bought it.

title: How to (Accidentally) Spot a British Pakistani Aunty. Tip #5
body: Ask about the trip back and it's a military operation. Booked in January, six suitcases, four of them gifts, a list her sister updated by voice note over eight weeks. Excess baggage paid without a word of complaint. It's a sealed deal if somebody requested a specific brand they saw online and would not be talked out of it.

title: How to (Accidentally) Spot a British Pakistani Aunty. Tip #6
body: Ask about her children and count the seconds before a profession appears. A doctor, a dentist, or one in law and one who is "in business," which is doing an enormous amount of work in that sentence. It's a sealed deal if she can name every cousin's degree and the university and has never once been asked.

title: How to (Accidentally) Spot a British Pakistani Aunty. Tip #7
body: Watch what happens when someone in the community is ill. Within a day there is a rota, food, and four families at the hospital. The same network that gossips relentlessly also functions better than most institutions. It's a sealed deal if a family has been fed by neighbours for a fortnight and nobody organised it formally.

title: How to (Accidentally) Spot a British Pakistani Aunty. Tip #8
body: Ask about the house back home and there is one, half-built, in Lahore or Mirpur, and it has been three years from finished since 2014. Money goes into it every year. Nobody in the family has lived in it or will. It's a sealed deal if a photograph of that house gets shown to visitors with total sincerity.
